subject: understand dimension of extraconstr in f()

messages.author: 80b903b54c9cf4bd
messages.subject: understand dimension of extraconstr in f()
parts:
Hi, I want to add a spatio-temporal interaction term in my model, something like this
f(ID.area.year, model='generic0', Cmatrix=R, rankdef=r.def,constr=TRUE,
    hyper=list(prec=list(prior=sdunif)),
    extraconstr = list(A=A.constr, e=rep(0, SS+TT))
  )
But I am not sure what's the dimension of f() as mentioned in the documentation of extraconstr .
Basically, in my data, for example, I have 10 areas, 5 years, the distinct interaction term will have dimension 10*5=50. However, my problem is that on each area in each year, there will be multiple responses, unlike in disease mapping problems, there is a single response.  So the dimension of my data will be, for example 1000. Each area, year, area.year will appear multiple times. The spatial, temporal or spatio-temporal interaction are just some random effects in my model.

So in summary, there are only 50 unique values of ID.area.year. But my data has 1000 observations, so the size of the column ID.area.year is my data.frame is 1000.

My questions are:
1.  Is that appropriate to use the f() model directly with no modification? Like a CAR prior, or bym prior? Even if there are multiple responses on same area.

2. There is an argument constr=TRUE for the intrinsic models. When the sum-to-zero constraint is used, is this applied on unique values of the latent effect (eg: area_1, ..., area_10), or applied on the whole column in the data.frame (eg: sum(df$ID.area) = 0 while length(df$ID.area)=1000)? 

3. A similar question when adding extra constraints through matrix A.constr. Currently I'm assume the number of columns of A.constr equals the number of unique values of the latent effect. Is that correct? Should it be the size of the data.frame?

Hope I had clarified my problems.

Best,

Jiang

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] understand dimension of extraconstr in f()

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] understand dimension of extraconstr in f()
parts:
If you have multiple observations in each area, its a matter of modelling.  If you observe the *same* field multiple times, then you can just replicate id.area, like

id.area = c(…, 3,3, ….)

And same with ‘x’

If you have observations of also another realisation of the field, then you can use replicate, to get another field with the same hypearparameters. Like

id.area = c(1:n, 1:n)
r=rep(1:2, each=n)
And then f(id.area, model=“besag”, replicate=r)

Like if you have annual data, and replicate is the annual random effect. 

H

Basically, in my data, for example, I have 10 areas, 5 years, the distinct interaction term will have dimension 10*5=50. However, my problem is that on each area in each year, there will be multiple responses, unlike in disease mapping problems, there is a single response.  So the dimension of my data will be, for example 1000. Each area, year, area.year will appear multiple times. The spatial, temporal or spatio-temporal interaction are just some random effects in my model.

So in summary, there are only 50 unique values of ID.area.year. But my data has 1000 observations, so the size of the column ID.area.year is my data.frame is 1000.

My questions are:
1.  Is that appropriate to use the f() model directly with no modification? Like a CAR prior, or bym prior? Even if there are multiple responses on same area.

2. There is an argument constr=TRUE for the intrinsic models. When the sum-to-zero constraint is used, is this applied on unique values of the latent effect (eg: area_1, ..., area_10), or applied on the whole column in the data.frame (eg: sum(df$ID.area) = 0 while length(df$ID.area)=1000)? 

3. A similar question when adding extra constraints through matrix A.constr. Currently I'm assume the number of columns of A.constr equals the number of unique values of the latent effect. Is that correct? Should it be the size of the data.frame?

Hope I had clarified my problems.

Best,

Jiang
